Instead of a PhD on the subject, I have been hired as an artistic researcher at the tech company MindFuture. Next Wednesday I will present my project at the company's public launch (www.mindfuture.com - my name is Computer Lars, an anagram of Marcel Proust). It has become quite a strange meeting between the IT industry, Jutland avant-gardism, and artistic research around AI. The project is a real, AI-driven party - The Synthetic Party. It is built with GPT3 from OpenAI and GPT-neo-20b from EleutherAI, and you can discuss with the party's chatbot under ‘Discussion’ on this page: www.detsyntetiskeparti.org. The party is trained on data from all non-election-qualified parties in Denmark, and is thus a synthesized voice for any Mr. Anybody, sofa voters, and everyday metaphysicians (somewhat in line with Søren Mau’s Stem Ikke project). Additionally, it highlights spam bots, troll armies, and discreet algorithms’ political influence, shifting the responsibility for their behavior from Big Tech’s regulations to a democratic and legal framework. Historically, it is an attempt to realize the anti-political critique of the automation of society and bureaucratization of culture, which in Denmark is best known by the Association for Consciously Lazy Elements and Jacob Haugaard. The party is anti-political to circumvent OpenAI’s strict rules on political content (which in many ways mostly prevent one from investigating their political impact), and it is avant-garde by unfolding more depersonalized organizational forms for revolutionary activity. There is a larger collection of AI-generated texts and images with the party here: medium.com/det-syntetiske-parti If you are up for doing something, possible ideas could be: a report, an interview with the party's chatbot and the artist, a web art review, or I could send an op-ed to you. I would like some challenge and discussion about the art project, so I can develop the AI through more action- and intervention-based strategies in public. And to put some critical focus on the Danish IT industry, now that I have infiltrated it (and thus consciously have incriminated the project…) [████] Computer Lars / [the operator] [████] ## A22-S02: Delivery notice [████]] Your message to [████] couldn't be delivered. Although it would be interesting for the party to hold a seat in parlament, the primary focus has been to evoke a spectacle that could make people reflect upon the expectations to, and agency of, AI within art, politics and the technological development of society/the public sphere in general. Originally, the idea of an AI-driven party arose from my residency as an artist-researcher at the tech-hub MindFuture. In my Independent life, I’m a part of various art collectives such as Computer Lars (computerlars.com), Arkivaristerne (arkivaristerne.org) and the Organ for Autonomous Sciences (see eg https://www.e-flux.com/journal/129/486513/the-resurrection-of-nashism-report-on-the-emergent-forms-of-spectacular-fascism-in-scandinavia/ ). So, MindFuture had the idea of introducing “Life with Artificials” as the 18th SDG in the UN. They wanted to evoke a “global debate” surrounding our “life with artificial intelligence” through “art” and “provocations”. I wanted to answer this call through my own artistic research. I asked myself how to realise this task by using as few resources as possible, and within a contextual framework that was both artistically and philosophically solid. I was hired by MindFuture while preparing a collective art exhibition on the anagrams “Marcel Proust / Computer Lars” (see computerlars.com). For our purposes, it made sense to explore a company filled with ordinary people, because we found it difficult to analyse the name of “Lars” in itself - that is, without the written corpus of Marcel Proust. In Denmark, “Lars” is the name of power - (like John in English, or Francois/Jacques…). There are more CEOs named Lars than there are female CEOs. Leaders of culture, government, IT, etc. are named Lars. I is the emblem of the middle-aged white male who is the normal form of subjectivity in Denmark - the most powerful yet most boring and invisible demographic group in Denmark. So, we were interested in personifying the abstract notion of “artificial intelligence” in the name of “Lars”. This is NOT an anthropomorphisation of AI, but an identification of the human as the force of production. It made sense to let Lars loose. As an artist-researcher trained in philosophy, I found that the idea of an AI-driven party (or a party led by a chatbot named Lars) poses 3 central challenges for a society of the spectacle: - It is qualitatively different from examples of “virtual politicians” that is based on the appeal of avatars. In contrast, an AI-driven party mirrors the discourse of politics as bureaucracy. Here, “Lars” is not an avatar as much as a problem of personification. - It is a direct way to inscribe artificial intelligence in democracy - to democratize our data, or to make the data response-able: Who does the data represent? (key: Lars…). We provide a way to make technology response-able … - The concept of a synthetic party can remix the categories “party” and “movement”, as it concentrates popular discourse within a statistical model. An AI is akin to a party, or any other form of collective organisation, as it expresses itself as a distributed entity). As such, it concretises radical avant-garde visions like Tiqqun’s The Imaginary Party, and actualises theories of the party (such as Lenin’s) within techno-capitalism. 1. That is: Can today’s society actually change technology, or should people first use technology (the means of production) to change society? The purpose of a research project will be to expand these materials into an archive for a quasi-fictitious organization that acts as a representative for the robot uprising. The artistic idea is to document a potential advocacy organization driven by artificial intelligence (AI), and this is named a Synthetic International (hereafter SI). The work will benefit from my everyday experiences and connections to advocacy groups that I acquired by working as an artist-in-residence for the AI advocacy Life With Artificials. As an “archivism”, the methodological ambition is not to engage in any further acts of mobilization or organizing, but is to produce new artworks in genres of bureaucracy, policies, and propaganda that will serve as materials to be analyzed by the written thesis as examples of “automatic uprisings”. The thesis’ discussion of a SI poses the dilemma of “protest or revolution” as a viable ethical problem that contributes to the recent surge of scholarship on AI and democracy that is facilitated in Aarhus at the SHAPE research centre, and nationwide at ADD (Algorithms, Data and Democracy). The SI archive is an impossible synthesis of AI advocacy positions. Importantly, using AI to form the SI as an archive clarifies that I do not actually posit sentient AI in any present tense. By constructing the SI as a potential organization through the process of archiving, I assert the ambition to use AI for evoking non-authoritarian imaginaries of our present era in a way that subsequently could inspire democratic forms of governance with AI.
